title: a CLAUDE.md, .claude/CLAUDE.md or CLAUDE.local.md is never written: only AGENTS.md gets the block, a Claude file that does not import AGENTS.md gets a warning, and --remove restores AGENTS.md
source: intended: owner decision (v0.2): JITSO writes instruction blocks to AGENTS.md files only, never to CLAUDE.md
intended: owner decision (v0.3): a CLAUDE.md or .claude/CLAUDE.md that does not import AGENTS.md is a warning, because Claude Code reads only it
intent: INTENDED behavior (setup instructions writes AGENTS.md only). Whatever Claude Code memory file the checkout has, as long as it holds no JITSO block, `setup instructions --yes` creates `AGENTS.md` with the block, does not name the Claude file in the preview or the result, and leaves that file byte for byte. Claude Code reads only `CLAUDE.md` or `.claude/CLAUDE.md` when one exists, and resolves an import relative to the file that holds it, so a `CLAUDE.md` without `@AGENTS.md` (one that only quotes it in code does not count) and a `.claude/CLAUDE.md` without `@../AGENTS.md` get one warning on stderr naming the line to add; a file that imports AGENTS.md and a `CLAUDE.local.md` (not looked at) get none. `--remove --yes` deletes the created `AGENTS.md`, warns about nothing and still leaves the Claude file alone.
